meta.status: Ids match the Field Book (S-01 through S-10). S-06 microwave wire is PENDING. S-11 and S-12 are tab-only heights with no book number.

rules.title: Commercial branch circuits
rules.text: Commercial work: 20A minimum on every branch circuit (12 AWG copper minimum). No 15A branch circuits on commercial jobs.

rules.title: New gear is Siemens
rules.text: All new gear (panels, meter-mains, breakers, disconnects) is Siemens.

rules.title: Match the existing panel
rules.text: In an existing Square D panel, use Square D breakers listed for that panel. Don't mix brands.

rules.title: Wall receptacle height
rules.text: Receptacles: 18 in to the BOTTOM of the box when the plan is silent. When the plan states a height, the plan governs.

rules.title: Switch height
rules.text: Switches: 48 in to the center of the box when the plan is silent.

rules.title: Microwave circuit — PENDING
rules.text: PENDING RULING. The microwave gets its own dedicated 20A circuit. Mike Holt has not ruled the wire: 12 AWG copper versus 10 AWG CCA. Until that ruling, do not treat either size as the company standard. Both can meet 240.4(D) — 12 AWG copper is capped at 20A, and 10 AWG CCA is capped at 25A. The lead decides for the job. If the plan or the nameplate states a size, that statement governs.
rules.status: PENDING RULING — 12 AWG copper vs 10 AWG CCA

rules.title: Dual-function breakers
rules.text: Every 120V breaker is a dual-function AFCI/GFCI breaker. Points marked GFI on the plan get a standard tamper-resistant receptacle protected by that breaker. The crew does not pick a GFCI receptacle for protection.

rules.title: Dryer circuit
rules.text: Dryer circuit: Siemens Q230GF, 30A 2-pole GFCI breaker. Ground-fault protection is required for the 125–250V laundry receptacle under NEC 2020 210.8(A).

rules.title: Meter and panel back to back
rules.text: Meter and panel go back to back where the house allows: meter outside, panel inside directly behind it. The 110.26 working space in front of the panel still has to be there.

rules.title: Wire — copper and CCA
rules.text: Branch circuits are copper by default: 14 AWG on 15A, 12 AWG on 20A. When copper-clad aluminum (CCA) is used, go one AWG size larger (12 AWG on 15A, 10 AWG on 20A), because Table 310.16 rates CCA in the aluminum column. Ordinary 15/20A device screw terminals are fine with CCA. CO/ALR is for plain aluminum. Wire nuts and lugs for CCA must say AL-CU. Push-in holes are 14 AWG solid copper only. Never backstab. The lead picks the wire. The microwave wire is not part of this default — it is PENDING under S-06.

rules.title: Garage outlet height
rules.text: Garage outlets at 48 in to center. This height is a Sharma tab rule. It is not S-04 or S-05.

rules.title: Outdoor outlet height
rules.text: Outdoor outlets at 24 in above grade. This height is a Sharma tab rule. It is not S-04 (wall receptacles, 18 in to the bottom of the box).
